# Phantom

> Rust HTTP client that connects the way a chosen browser does. Phantom reproduces the TLS ClientHello, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 behavior, request fields, and WebSocket openings of Chrome 154, Edge 153, Brave 154, Opera 135, and Firefox 156; QUIC and HTTP/3 for the four Chromium-based browsers only; client hints for the same four (Firefox sends none); and TCP socket options from browser source for Chrome and, partly, Firefox. Edge, Brave, and Opera have no TCP recipe. Phantom never falls back to another protocol or route. Package `phantom-http`, library crate `phantom`. Pre-1.0 and not on crates.io; depend on a pinned git revision.

When you use Phantom as a dependency, a git checkout of the pinned revision sits under `~/.cargo/git/checkouts/`. Its `docs/` directory matches the version you build against. Prefer those files over what you remember about Phantom: the API changes between commits.

## Rules

- Build a `ClientProfile` from the recipes of one browser version, as the examples show. Edge 153, Brave 154, and Opera 135 use the Chromium 154 HTTP/2, WebSocket, QUIC, and HTTP/3 recipes; their captures match them on every compared field, so the pairing is one browser. The Edge, Brave, and Opera request templates need your `User-Agent`, and Brave's also need your `Accept-Language` (one of `en-US,en;q=0.5` to `q=0.9`, kept per session).
- Do not hand-write TLS, HTTP/2, QUIC, or HTTP/3 settings to imitate a browser. Use the recipe functions in `phantom::profile::{brave, chromium, edge, firefox, opera}`.
- Pick the protocol on every request: `HttpProtocol::Http1`, `Http2`, or `Http3` with `get` or `request`, or `get_negotiated` to let TLS ALPN choose HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
- Phantom never falls back. An unsupported protocol, route, or proxy returns a typed error; handle it instead of retrying with a different protocol.
- Redirects, retries, timeouts, cookies, Alt-Svc, and content decoding are off until you enable them on the `ClientBuilder` or request.
- Connection counts and waits default to browser values: one HTTP/2 connection per origin and route, the profile's HTTP/1.1 bound. Raising them (`max_http2_connections_per_origin`, `negotiated_setup_wait_limit`, and the others in the performance guide) is visible to a server. Phantom does no request pacing or rate limiting; schedule requests yourself.
- Phantom adds no browser request fields. Prepare a captured `RequestTemplate` once with `PreparedRequestTemplate::new` and pass it to `RequestBuilder::template` to send `User-Agent`, `Accept`, and `Sec-Fetch-*` in browser order. To an `http://` origin that is not loopback or `localhost`, a template leaves out `Sec-Fetch-*` and sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate`, and no client hints are sent, as browsers do. The built-in WebSocket recipes follow the same rule for a `ws://` opening: `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate` to a named origin, and Firefox's `Sec-Fetch-*` fields only to a trustworthy one.
- Header order is part of the fingerprint. Add fields in the order you want them sent; do not sort or deduplicate them.
- `RequestErrorKind` and `BuildErrorKind` are non-exhaustive; every `match` needs a fallback arm.
- Requests need a Tokio runtime with I/O and time enabled.
- Cargo features `cookies`, `https-records` (HTTP/3 discovery from HTTPS DNS records, and for the Chrome 154 and Brave 154 recipes Encrypted Client Hello from them, which can hold a direct TLS handshake up to 50 ms), `sse`, `websocket`, `websocket-deflate`, and `serde` (cookie-jar snapshots, with `cookies`) are off by default; `full` enables all of them. `diagnostics` (TLS key log and QUIC qlog files) is also off by default and not part of `full`, because a key log decrypts the client's traffic.
- A cookie snapshot from `Client::export_cookies` holds cookie values, which are credentials. `Client::import_cookies` rejects the whole snapshot if one entry is invalid, and never replaces a cookie the jar already holds.
- Read a response body to the end, or with `collect_with_limit`, when you want the connection reused.

## Guides

- [Using the client](docs/guides/client.md): client policies, protocols, fields, bodies, trailers, timeouts
- [Responses and errors](docs/guides/responses.md): ordered response fields, `ResponseInfo`, bounded bodies, error kinds
- [Browser profiles](docs/guides/profiles.md): choose a built-in profile, build a custom one
- [Request templates and client hints](docs/guides/request-templates.md): a browser's request fields in its order, and client hints
- [Routes and proxies](docs/guides/routes-and-proxies.md): routes, HTTP proxies, proxy authentication, trust roots
- [SOCKS5 and CONNECT-UDP proxies](docs/guides/socks-and-connect-udp.md): SOCKS5 tunnels and UDP ASSOCIATE, and HTTP/3 through CONNECT-UDP
- [Retries and replays](docs/guides/retries.md): when Phantom sends a request again
- [Connections and client state](docs/guides/connections-and-state.md): pools, the address cache, sessions, clearing learned state
- [Redirects](docs/guides/redirects.md): opt-in bounded redirects
- [Cookies](docs/guides/cookies.md): the `cookies` feature, snapshots, and cookie-field placement
- [HTTP/3 and Alt-Svc](docs/guides/http3.md): exact HTTP/3, early data, and opt-in Alt-Svc upgrade
- [HTTP/3 discovery](docs/guides/http3-discovery.md): Alt-Svc racing, HTTPS DNS records, and Alt-Svc snapshots
- [Content decoding](docs/guides/content-decoding.md): opt-in decompression
- [Tune throughput and latency](docs/guides/performance.md): concurrency bounds, extra HTTP/2 connections per origin, wait limits, and what each lets a server observe; Phantom does no request pacing
- [Server-sent events](docs/guides/sse.md): the `sse` feature
- [WebSocket](docs/guides/websocket.md): the `websocket` feature over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
- [WebSocket fields and compression](docs/guides/websocket-fields.md): caller-ordered openings, and the `websocket-deflate` feature
- [Adding Phantom to a project](docs/guides/downstream.md): git and path dependencies
- [Coming from reqwest](docs/guides/coming-from-reqwest.md): reqwest concepts mapped to Phantom, and behaviors that differ
- [Troubleshooting](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md): error kinds mapped to causes and fixes
- [Examples](crates/phantom/examples/README.md): runnable programs, one per guide task
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): breaking changes between commits, each with a migration note

- API: `cargo doc -p phantom-http --all-features --no-deps --open`
